description: Review signals for common interface quality problems. Findings require context and are not automatic failures.

signals: repeated card wrappers without distinct grouping
antiPatterns.falsePositive: Cards are appropriate for independently actionable or comparable entities.
antiPatterns.remedy: Use spacing, typography, dividers or open layout where grouping is unnecessary.

signals: generic headline, stock visual and undifferentiated CTA
antiPatterns.falsePositive: A conventional hero may be appropriate for a familiar audience or constrained brand.
antiPatterns.remedy: Tie the focal message and visual evidence to the actual product or audience.

signals: multiple decorative gradients competing with content
antiPatterns.falsePositive: A controlled gradient can be a legitimate brand asset or focal surface.
antiPatterns.remedy: Use gradients only when they reinforce hierarchy or brand identity.

signals: many competing accents, badges, borders or effects
antiPatterns.falsePositive: Dense operational interfaces may need many simultaneous status cues.
antiPatterns.remedy: Prioritize information by importance and reduce redundant decoration.

signals: large empty regions that separate related content without purpose
antiPatterns.falsePositive: Whitespace can be intentional in editorial or premium brand work.
antiPatterns.remedy: Check reading flow, viewport context and section relationships before reducing space.

signals: weak distinction between headings, body, metadata and actions
antiPatterns.falsePositive: A deliberately restrained typographic system may use a narrow scale.
antiPatterns.remedy: Strengthen hierarchy through scale, weight, line length and spacing.

signals: same card grid or split layout repeated across unrelated sections
antiPatterns.falsePositive: Repeated patterns can improve scanning when content is genuinely parallel.
antiPatterns.remedy: Vary composition when the content purpose changes.

signals: control-like element has no meaningful action or state
antiPatterns.falsePositive: Static examples may intentionally depict controls as illustrations.
antiPatterns.remedy: Implement a real action/state or render it as non-interactive content.

signals: desktop columns, controls or type become cramped at narrow widths
antiPatterns.falsePositive: Some specialist tools legitimately require horizontal data navigation.
antiPatterns.remedy: Reflow content, preserve usable targets and provide intentional overflow behavior.

signals: text or meaningful controls may lack sufficient contrast
antiPatterns.falsePositive: Opaque color-pair checks cannot evaluate images, gradients, overlays or alpha compositing.
antiPatterns.remedy: Measure actual rendered foreground/background states and inspect focus and disabled states.
